newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia repeats De Beers deal to proceed.
newsitem.headline: Russia repeats De Beers deal to proceed.

text.p: A senior Russian diamond official reiterated on Thursday that a delayed deal between Russia and South African De Beers would be signed in spite of a government investigation into the Russian partner in the deal.

Vladimir Piskunov, head of the precious metals and stones department at the Industry Ministry, told Interfax news agency that various ministries were examining charges against Almazy-Rossii Sahkha (ARS), Russia's main diamond producer and De Beers' negotiating partner, by the prosecutor-general's office.
Piskunov acknowledged that a trade agreement with De Beers was running behind schedule, but said he was convinced it would be signed.
The prosecutor-general's office accused ARS earlier this month of alleged financial irregularities.
ARS President Vyacheslav Shtyrov told Reuters last week the investigation would not harm the deal, which he expected to be signed by December.
ARS, which mines nearly all of Russia's diamonds and is its sole official exporter, reached a preliminary agreement with De Beers' to export rough gems under a memorandum signed in February.
The memorandum forms the basis of the final trade agreement which is awaiting signature by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
